Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')

strengths: The method addresses a useful computer vision problem: scalable dataset distillation through feature matching and per-class BatchNorm regularization, without unrolling network training.
Reported results are strong. At 50 images per class, WMDD achieves 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet versus 48.7% for the strongest listed baseline, and 57.6% on ImageNet-1K versus 53.5% (Table 1).

The factorial ablation supports the combined design: on ImageNet-1K, Wasserstein matching with PCBN reaches 38.1%, versus 36.4% for cross-entropy with PCBN (Table 4). Cross-architecture experiments also demonstrate useful transfer to other ResNets and vision transformers.

The manuscript provides pseudocode, hyperparameters, repeated-run results, and a code link. It credits the underlying transport solver, inversion methods, and datasets, and acknowledges that distillation can preserve source-data biases.
weaknesses: The central formulation has an unaddressed connection to classical quantization. With one input distribution, squared Euclidean cost, and freely optimized weights, Eqs. (5)–(8) reduce to minimizing the average squared distance to the nearest prototype: the k-means objective. The paper neither discusses this equivalence nor compares against k-means prototypes within the same image-synthesis pipeline. This leaves the originality and necessity of the proposed transport machinery insufficiently established.

The baseline comparisons contain an important unexplained discrepancy. At 10 IPC on ImageNet-1K, Table 4's CE+BN configuration achieves 35.9%, whereas Table 1 reports 21.3% for SRe2L. These configurations are not necessarily identical, but their relationship and the source of this large difference need explanation before the headline improvement can be attributed confidently to the proposed method.

The metric comparison does not convincingly isolate the metric. At 1 IPC, the squared-Wasserstein prototype is the feature mean, making Eq. (12) equivalent to linear-MMD mean matching under identical feature extraction. Figure 4's large difference therefore requires explanation through the remaining pipeline differences. Removing augmentations and FKD does not establish matched encoders and regularization. Appendix B supplies standard separate risk bounds, without demonstrating a tighter bound for the implemented method.

Algorithm 2 leaves consequential implementation ambiguities. It updates the weights after computing the transport plan, then reuses that plan for the position update, although its marginals correspond to the previous weights. Equation (11) also divides by weights that simplex projection can set to zero. The handling of these cases and the precise use of learned weights during FKD should be specified to make the algorithm reproducible and support its convergence claims.

The efficiency evidence only partially supports the practical savings claimed. Table 3 evaluates memory and comparative runtime at 1 IPC on ImageNette; Table 5 adds Tiny ImageNet timings. ImageNet-1K measurements with clearly itemized teacher training, feature extraction, prototype computation, synthesis, and relabeling costs are missing.
